commands.pickDate_comment: Command palette entry, shown after the plugin name, so keep it short. Opens the calendar on the date at the cursor, or writes a new date in at the cursor when there is none. 'Pick' is the reader choosing a day from a calendar, not selecting text.

notes.notes_comment: Heading of the settings section covering how a date behaves in a note: what opens the calendar, and what is drawn around a date under the pointer.
notes.heading: Dates in a note

commandOnly.name_comment: Small line at the top of the 'Dates in a note' section, shown only when both the double-click and the hover icon are switched off, so nothing in a note opens the calendar any more. {{command}} is replaced by the name of the Pick a date command, taken from commands.pickDate so it matches the command palette whatever the command is called — keep the marker, and quote it with your language's quotation marks. Keep 'Note:', or your language's equivalent, as an opener. For 'command palette', use the words your language's Obsidian uses for it. The reader chose this, so word it as a fact, not a warning.
commandOnly.name: Note: Only “{{command}}” from the command palette opens the calendar

calendar.calendar_comment: Heading of the settings section covering what the calendar itself shows once open.
calendar.heading: Calendar

doubleClick.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle that lets a double-click on a date open the calendar.
doubleClick.name: Double-click
doubleClick.desc: Double-click a date to open the calendar.

hoverIcon.name_comment: Settings row label for the dropdown controlling the small icon that appears beside a date while the pointer is over it.
hoverIcon.name: Icon on hover
hoverIcon.desc_comment: Description under that dropdown. {{icon}} is replaced by the icon itself, drawn inline — keep the marker, and put it where the icon reads naturally in your language.
hoverIcon.desc: Click the {{icon}} that appears when the pointer is over a date.

options.off_comment: Dropdown option: no icon appears at all.
options.left_comment: Dropdown option: the icon appears before the date.
options.right_comment: Dropdown option: the icon appears after the date.

taskEmoji.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle that makes one of the Tasks plugin's date emoji the way into the calendar for the date written after it. {{emojis}} is replaced by the list of those emoji — keep the marker, and keep it in brackets. "Tasks" is the name of another Obsidian plugin: leave it as it is, and use the plural form your language's Obsidian uses for plugin names.
taskEmoji.name: Tasks plugin emojis ({{emojis}})
taskEmoji.desc_comment: Description under that toggle. "one" means one of the emoji listed in the label above. The second sentence says what the reader gives up: a date with an emoji in front of it is opened through the emoji, so the hover icon is not drawn on it.
taskEmoji.desc: Click one to open the calendar. Those dates get no hover icon.

hoverFrame.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle that draws an outline around a date and its icon while the pointer is over them.
hoverFrame.name: Outline on hover

weekNumbers.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle adding a week-number column to the calendar.
weekNumbers.name: Week numbers

weekStart.name_comment: Settings row label for the dropdown choosing which day a week starts on in the calendar.
weekStart.name: First day of the week

writesPreview.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle showing, in the calendar, the exact text a pick will write into the note.
writesPreview.name: Preview the new date

quickDates.heading_comment: Title of the settings page holding the configurable shortcut buttons shown under the calendar, and the label of the row that opens it.
quickDates.heading: Quick dates
quickDates.description_comment: One line of explanation at the top of that page. "Today" is the name of the permanent button that is always there.
quickDates.description: They sit under the calendar, after Today.
quickDates.shortcuts_comment: Heading over the table of four shortcut slots, separating them from the switch above.
quickDates.shortcutsDesc_comment: Line under that heading. The shortcuts sit on one row under the calendar and keep the width their names need; when the row runs out of space they are cut off at the end with an ellipsis.
quickDates.shortcutsDesc: Keep names short. The calendar cuts off whatever does not fit the row.
quickDates.sample_comment: Heading over the calendar shown at the foot of the page, which is what the reader's own settings currently produce.
quickDates.show_comment: Settings row label for the switch that hides the quick-date row without clearing what is in it.
quickDates.none_comment: Value shown on the Quick dates row when no slot is filled.
quickDates.off_comment: Value shown on the Quick dates row when the switch is off, whatever the slots hold.
quickDates.empty_comment: Shown in the chooser and on an unfilled slot. The dashes are decorative; drop them if they read oddly in your language.
quickDates.custom_comment: Last entry in the chooser, below the presets. Opens the builder for a shortcut of your own.
quickDates.alias_comment: Placeholder in the text field setting a shortcut's button text. For a preset it may be left empty, and the preset's own name is used.
quickDates.edit_comment: Hover label on the pencil button that reopens the builder for a shortcut of your own.

columns.rule_comment: Column header over the chooser on the quick-dates page, where a preset or a shortcut of your own is picked.
columns.name_comment: Column header over the field holding the text that appears on the button.
columns.name: Name
columns.meaning_comment: Column header over the plain-language reading of each shortcut, such as "Today → 7 days on".

short.tomorrow_comment: Short form shown on the button in the calendar and used as the name field's placeholder. Keep it short — a long one widens the calendar.
short.yesterday_comment: Short form on the button. Keep it short.
short.inSevenDays_comment: Short form on the button. Keep it short.
short.nextMonday_comment: Short form on the button, abbreviating the weekday the way your language does in a calendar. Keep it short.
short.nextFriday_comment: Short form on the button, abbreviating the weekday the way your language does in a calendar. Keep it short.
short.endOfThisWeek_comment: Short form on the button: end of this week. An abbreviation of your language's own words for it, three or four letters if that works — it sits on a small button. Unmarked means counted from today, against the "That …" forms counted from the date being edited.
short.startOfNextWeek_comment: Short form on the button: the start of next week. Keep it short.
short.endOfThisMonth_comment: Short form on the button: end of this month. Keep it short.
short.startOfNextMonth_comment: Short form on the button: the start of next month. Keep it short.
short.endOfThisQuarter_comment: Short form on the button: end of this quarter. Keep it short.
short.dayLater_comment: Short form on the button: one day after the date being edited. The plus marks the family counted from that date rather than from today.
short.sevenDaysLater_comment: Short form on the button: seven days after the date being edited.
short.fourteenDaysLater_comment: Short form on the button: fourteen days after the date being edited.
short.monthLater_comment: Short form on the button: one month after the date being edited.
short.startOfThatWeek_comment: Short form on the button: the start of the week the edited date falls in. "That" marks the family counted from that date rather than from today.
short.endOfThatWeek_comment: Short form on the button: the end of the week the edited date falls in.
short.startOfThatMonth_comment: Short form on the button: the start of the month the edited date falls in.
short.endOfThatMonth_comment: Short form on the button: the end of the month the edited date falls in.

presets.tomorrow_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the next day.
presets.yesterday_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the previous day.
presets.inSevenDays_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today. The wording "In …" marks every preset that counts from today, against "… later" for the ones counting from the date being edited — keep that contrast in your language.
presets.nextMonday_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the coming Monday. On a Monday it means the following one.
presets.nextFriday_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the coming Friday. On a Friday it means the following one.
presets.endOfThisWeek_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the last day of the current week, which depends on the first-day-of-the-week setting. "This" marks a preset counted from today, against "that" for one counted from the date being edited.
presets.startOfNextWeek_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the first day of the following week.
presets.endOfThisMonth_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the last day of the current month.
presets.startOfNextMonth_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the first day of the following month.
presets.endOfThisQuarter_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from today: the last day of the current three-month quarter.
presets.dayLater_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from the date being edited rather than from today. "… later" marks that whole family.
presets.sevenDaysLater_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from the date being edited: a week after it.
presets.fourteenDaysLater_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from the date being edited: a fortnight after it.
presets.monthLater_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from the date being edited: a month after it.
presets.startOfThatWeek_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from the date being edited: the first day of the week that date falls in. "That" marks a preset counted from the date being edited, against "this" for one counted from today.
presets.endOfThatWeek_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from the date being edited: the last day of the week that date falls in.
presets.startOfThatMonth_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from the date being edited: the first day of the month that date falls in.
presets.endOfThatMonth_comment: Preset shortcut, counted from the date being edited: the last day of the month that date falls in.

anchors.today_comment: First piece of the plain-language reading of a shortcut, when it counts from today. The pieces are joined by arrows, e.g. "Today → 2 weeks on".
anchors.date_comment: First piece of the plain-language reading of a shortcut, when it counts from the date being edited.

steps.forward_comment: One piece of a shortcut's reading: moving forward by an amount. {{amount}} is replaced by a counted phrase such as "2 weeks". Keep the marker.
steps.back_comment: One piece of a shortcut's reading: moving backwards by an amount. {{amount}} is replaced by a counted phrase such as "2 weeks".
steps.amount_d_one_comment: A counted amount of days, placed inside the two phrases above. Add or remove plural forms as your language needs; every form your language uses must be present.
steps.weekdayNext_comment: One piece of a shortcut's reading: the coming Monday, Tuesday and so on. {{day}} is replaced by the day's name in your language, supplied by the date library.
steps.weekdayPrevious_comment: One piece of a shortcut's reading: the most recent Monday, Tuesday and so on.
steps.weekdayNth_one_comment: One piece of a shortcut's reading: counting forward over several of the same weekday, as in "2 Mondays on". {{count}} is the number and {{day}} the day's name, which arrives singular from the date library. Add the plural forms your language needs, and word them so the day name can stay as it comes.
steps.weekdayThis_comment: One piece of a shortcut's reading: the nearest such weekday, today included if today is already it. It stands against the "next {{day}}" line above, which always moves.

edges.SoW_comment: One of the eight period edges, offered in a dropdown and shown in a shortcut's reading. The week's first day, which depends on the first-day-of-the-week setting.
edges.EoW_comment: The week's last day, which depends on the first-day-of-the-week setting.
edges.SoQ_comment: The first day of the three-month quarter.
edges.EoQ_comment: The last day of the three-month quarter.

modal.nameDesc_comment: Description under the name field in the dialog for a shortcut of your own. It is the text on a button in a small calendar, so a long one is clipped.
modal.title_comment: Title of the dialog for writing a shortcut of your own.
modal.title: Custom quick date
modal.name_comment: Label of the field holding the text that will appear on the button.
modal.name: Name
modal.rule_comment: Label of the field holding the shortcut's rule, which is typed with help from a list of suggestions.
modal.hint_comment: Shown under an empty rule field. "today" and "date" are typed exactly as they appear here, in English, in every language — leave them as they are.
modal.hint: Start with “today” or “date”, then add steps.

starts.today_comment: Shown beside "today" in the list under the rule field, saying what choosing it does. The reader may never have met the field before.
starts.date_comment: Shown beside "date" in the list under the rule field. It means the date the calendar was opened on, which is the one being edited.
starts.date: Start from the date in the note

modal.done_comment: First entry in the suggestion list once the rule is complete. Choosing it closes the list and keeps what has been typed. The dashes are decorative; drop them if they read oddly.
modal.testDate_comment: Label of the field holding a date to try the shortcut against. It stands in for both today and the date being edited, so the reader can see what the shortcut would do on any day.
modal.pick_comment: Hover label on the button beside the test date, which opens a calendar to choose one.
modal.badTestDate_comment: Shown when the test date cannot be read. {{pattern}} is replaced by the reader's first date format, such as YYYY-MM-DD. Keep the marker.
modal.badTestDate: The test date must be written {{pattern}}.

problems.anchor_comment: Error under the rule field: the rule does not begin with one of the two starting words. {{token}} is replaced by what was typed instead. "today" and "date" are typed in English in every language — leave them as they are, and keep the quotation marks your language uses.
problems.anchor: A rule must start with “today” or “date”, not “{{token}}”.
problems.steps_comment: Error under the rule field: the rule names a starting point but does nothing with it. "Today" here is the name of the permanent button under the calendar.
problems.steps: Add a step. “today” alone is already the Today button.
problems.minutes_comment: Error under the rule field, shown for a step such as +15m. Months are written with a capital M and minutes with a small m, which is the date library's own rule. Keep both letters as they are.
problems.minutes: m means minutes. Write M for months.
problems.reserved_comment: Error under the rule field: the step names a time of day, which this cannot pick yet. {{token}} is replaced by what was typed.
problems.reserved: “{{token}}” is a time, and the calendar picks dates.
problems.count_comment: Error under the rule field: the step names a real unit but is missing its sign or its number, or the number is out of range. {{token}} is replaced by what was typed; +2Mon is an example and stays as it is.
problems.count: “{{token}}” needs a sign and a number from 1 to 999, like +2Mon.
problems.token_comment: Error under the rule field: the step is not anything this understands. {{token}} is replaced by what was typed; the three examples are typed the same way in every language, so leave them as they are.
problems.token: “{{token}}” is not a step. Steps look like +1w, Mon or EoM.

modal.cancel_comment: Button that closes the dialog without keeping the shortcut.
modal.save_comment: Button that keeps the shortcut. Unavailable until it has a name and a rule that reads.

formats.heading_comment: Heading above the list of date formats the plugin looks for.
formats.heading: Date formats
formats.description_comment: The single line of explanation under the Date formats heading. 'Applied top to bottom' means that when two formats could both read the same text, the one higher in the list wins.
formats.description: The date formats Kalendae recognises in your notes, applied top to bottom.
formats.add_comment: Tooltip on the + button beside the Date formats heading, which opens a menu of formats to add.
formats.addCustom_comment: Last entry in the add menu, below the built-in formats. Opens a page for writing a format of your own.
formats.builtIn_comment: Hover label on the icon at the start of a format row that came with Kalendae. These formats cannot be edited, only removed or reordered.
formats.custom_comment: Hover label on the icon at the start of a format row the user wrote themselves. Contrasts with the built-in formats; these are the only ones with an edit button.
formats.newFormat_comment: Row label for a custom format that has been added but not yet given a pattern.
formats.unfinished_comment: Shown in place of the example on a format row whose pattern is incomplete or uses tokens Kalendae cannot read.
formats.edit_comment: Accessible label on the pencil button of a custom format row.
formats.delete_comment: Accessible label on the delete button of a format row.
formats.reorder_comment: Accessible label on the drag handle at the start of a format row.
formats.shadow_comment: Hover labels on the icon of a format row that an earlier format in the list beats to its dates. {{by}} is that earlier format's pattern, not translated. Three cases with three different answers: move the row up, remove one of the pair, or nothing at all.

shadow.move: Never used: {{by}} above it claims these dates first. Move this above it.
shadow.remove: Never used: {{by}} above it reads the same dates. Remove one.
shadow.shared: Shares dates with {{by}}. Where both fit, the one above wins.

modal.title_comment: Title of the dialog for writing or editing a custom date format.
modal.title: Custom format
modal.pattern_comment: Label for the text field holding the format pattern.
modal.required_comment: Shown after the name of a part a format cannot do without — year, month and day. Keep the brackets if they read naturally in your language.
modal.optional_comment: Shown after the name of a part a format may leave out, currently only the day of the week.
modal.columns_comment: Headings of the three columns in the token table: the tokens themselves, what each one writes, and whether the format being edited uses one.

groups.year_comment: Checklist row in the custom format dialog. The tokens beside it (YY, YYYY) are not translated. A tick appears when the format includes one of them.
groups.month_comment: Checklist row for the month tokens M, MM, MMM, MMMM.
groups.day_comment: Checklist row for the day-of-month tokens D, DD, Do.
groups.weekday_comment: Row for the weekday tokens d, dd, ddd, dddd. The only optional part, and the only row with no tick or cross beside it — there is nothing to satisfy.
groups.literal_comment: Last row of the token table, describing the punctuation between tokens rather than a part of a date. Everything that is not a letter is written into the note exactly as typed, so this row has no tick.

modal.warning_comment: Shown when a format holds nothing but numbers, as in YYYYMMDD, so a plain number in a note would match it. {{digits}} is how many digits it matches. A format with anything else in it — a separator, a month name — never shows this. Not an error, the format saves, so it is worded as advice.
modal.warning: Your format matches any {{digits}}-digit number. Consider adding separators.
modal.hint_comment: Shown where the error message goes while the format field is still empty. Not an error — nothing is wrong yet — so it is worded as a next step and shown in ordinary text rather than the error colour.
modal.hint: Write a format using the tokens above.

problem.adjacent_comment: Shown when a one-or-two-digit token touches another number and neither can be given a fixed width. {{first}} and {{second}} are the two tokens, not translated. Such a format cannot be read back reliably, so it cannot be saved.
problem.adjacent: Your format is ambiguous: {{first}} and {{second}} run together. Add a separator.
problem.adjacentWiden_comment: The same problem where one of the two tokens has a fixed-width form, as YYMDD does: {{from}} is M or D and {{to}} is MM or DD. Two ways out, and widening the token keeps the format's shape.
problem.adjacentWiden: Your format is ambiguous: {{first}} and {{second}} run together. Add a separator, or write {{from}} as {{to}}.
problem.adjacentWidenBoth_comment: The same problem where both tokens have a fixed-width form, as MDYYYY does. {{firstFixed}} and {{secondFixed}} are the widened tokens, in the same order as {{first}} and {{second}}.
problem.adjacentWidenBoth: Your format is ambiguous: {{first}} and {{second}} run together. Add a separator, or write them as {{firstFixed}} and {{secondFixed}}.

missing.year_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format has no year. The tokens are not translated.
missing.year: A format needs a year: add YY or YYYY.
missing.month_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format has no month. The tokens are not translated.
missing.month: A format needs a month: add M, MM, MMM or MMMM.
missing.day_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format has no day of the month. The tokens are not translated.
missing.day: A format needs a day: add D, DD or Do.

problem.unknownTokens_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format contains letters Kalendae has no token for. {{chars}} is those letters as typed, and may be more than one run of them separated by commas.
problem.brackets_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format holds a pair of square brackets. The date library reads anything between [ and ] as text to reproduce rather than as tokens, so such a format can never match a date and cannot be saved. Keep the [ and ] characters as they are and translate only the words around them. A bracket with no partner is fine and does not show this.

modal.cancel_comment: Button that closes the custom format dialog without keeping the format.
modal.save_comment: Button that keeps the custom format and closes the dialog. Unavailable while a required part is missing.

scopes.heading_comment: Label of the row that opens the page controlling which parts of a note are searched, and the title of that page.
scopes.heading: Sections to scan

text.name_comment: The first section on the Sections to scan page: the prose body of a note, as opposed to its headings, frontmatter, code or links. Always scanned, shown with a toggle that is on and cannot be moved.
text.name: Body text

headings.name_comment: Toggle label: markdown headings, the lines starting with #.
headings.name: Headings

frontmatter.name_comment: Toggle label: the YAML properties block at the top of a note.
frontmatter.name: Frontmatter

inlineCode.name_comment: Toggle label: short code spans written between single backticks.
inlineCode.name: Inline code

codeBlocks.name_comment: Toggle label: fenced code blocks written between triple backticks.
codeBlocks.name: Code blocks

wikilinks.name_comment: Toggle label: Obsidian's internal links, written between double square brackets.
wikilinks.name: Wikilinks

sample.heading_comment: Heading above the worked example at the bottom of the Sections to scan page.
sample.heading: Preview
sample.description_comment: Explains the example block on the Sections to scan page. Must make clear that the plugin never highlights dates in the user's own notes at all — not that it highlights them differently.
sample.description: An example note, shown for demonstration only. Kalendae does not highlight dates in your notes.
sample.detected_comment: Legend label for the colour marking dates the plugin would pick up.
sample.skipped_comment: Legend label for the colour marking dates the plugin would leave alone because their section is switched off.

picker.today_comment: Button under the calendar that sets the date to today and closes the picker. The only shortcut the picker ships with.
picker.weekColumn_comment: Heading of the optional week-number column, at the left edge of the calendar. Kept to two or three characters: the column is one number wide.
picker.prevMonth_comment: Screen-reader label for the single left chevron above the calendar. The button shows no text.
picker.nextMonth_comment: Screen-reader label for the single right chevron above the calendar.
picker.prevYear_comment: Screen-reader label for the double left chevron above the calendar, which steps a whole year.
picker.nextYear_comment: Screen-reader label for the double right chevron above the calendar.

notices.noEditor_comment: Notice shown when the Pick a date command runs somewhere there is no editor to read.
notices.noEditor: Open a note in editing view first.
